deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 28v is the back of the printed Göttingen doctoral diploma transcribed as the previous page (28r). What shows is the printed text of the front, seen in mirror image through the paper: the letters are reversed left-to-right. The ornamental 'GEORGII. V.' and the large names HENRICO ALBERTO ZACHARIAE, CAROLUS FRIDERIC. HENRICUS MARX and IOANNEM ROBERTUM BRANDMANN are clearly reversed. The 'L S' seal impression at the bottom is also seen from the back.

The document is the Göttingen medical faculty's promotion diploma. Dean Karl Friedrich Heinrich Marx, under Prorector Heinrich Albert Zachariae and in the reign of George V of Hanover, conferred the degree of Doctor of Medicine, Surgery and Obstetrics on Johann Robert Brandmann of Hamburg. The degree followed a public lecture 'de sectione caesarea post mortem' (on post-mortem Caesarean section), on 14 March 1866.

The paper was evidently reused or filed among Riemann's papers, probably as a wrapper or cover sheet. The next page carries an unrelated bibliographic note in Riemann's hand on Poggendorff's Annalen, dated Oct. 30, 1854. There are no formulas, derivations or mathematical marks. One very faint handwritten word, perhaps one or two words, appears above the line 'POST APPROBATAM ... PRAELECTIONE ...'. It is illegible and probably a manuscript correction or annotation on the diploma itself, not mathematics. There are also a tear and creases. Nothing on this page can be reconstructed mathematically.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is the mirror-image show-through on the back of a printed 1866 medical doctoral diploma, kept with Riemann's papers as scrap or a wrapper. It has no mathematical content.
transcription_corrections: The page is the verso, and all text is mirror-reversed show-through of the printed recto (28r); it is not independent text written on 28v.
Date: the mirrored image reads 'MDCCCLXVI' (1866), matching the recto, not 'MDCCCLXI[?]'.
'EXAMINE LEGITIMO' should read 'EXAMINE LEGITIMAM' (agreeing with SCIENTIAM), as on the recto.
'NEC NON DISSERTATIONE[?]' should read 'NECNON PRAELECTIONE' (the visible word length and letters match PRAELECTIONE).
'CUIUS REI HAS LITERAS TESTES' should read 'HUIUSQUE REI HAS LITERAS TESTES'.

The lines rendered as '[...]' are fully restorable from the recto. They are MAGNIDUCALIS LUXEMBURGICI ORDINIS QUERCICAE CORONAE CENTURIONE; AQUILAE RUBRAE BORUSSORUM ORDINIS EQUITE; COLLEGII QUOD DE IURE RESPONDET ASSESSORE; EQUES GUELPHICUS; REGI AB AULAE CONSILIIS; SOCIETATIS REGIAE SCIENTIARUM GOTTINGENSIS; NECNON COMPLURIUM SOCIETATUM LITERARIARUM SODALIS; HAMBURGENSEM.
'CAROLUS FRIDERICUS' appears in the print as the abbreviation 'CAROLUS. FRIDERIC.'.
The printer's line 'TYPIS EXPRESSIT OFFICINA ACADEMICA DIETERICHIANA' is not visibly shown through on this verso.
A faint handwritten word above the 'POST APPROBATAM...' line is not transcribed. It is illegible, and its handwriting is not identified.
